A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same MOFFlow research work, with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices. Retained material can be matched across appendix moves and equation renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original MOF structure-prediction, property, scalability, and self-assembly comparison results in Section 5.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds empirical batching, integration-step, and self-assembly analyses in Appendices D, G, and H.

M1.justification: The stated training loss changes from unsquared residuals in v1 Equation 10 to squared errors, log-map rotation residuals, and 1/(1-t)^2 weighting in v2 Equation 7. Appendix D also introduces batches containing multiple data instances instead of noise variants of one instance. The core rigid-body flow and architecture remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish whether the loss revision changed the implementation behind retained results.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same hypothetical MOF dataset from Boyd et al. and the same structure-prediction task. The added analyses reuse this coverage, including a test-set subset. Real-world datasets and building-block libraries are discussed but not newly evaluated.

E2.justification: v2 adds self-assembly to the building-block-count scalability comparison in Figure 8a; v1's corresponding block-count plot showed MOFFlow alone. Self-assembly was already evaluated for aggregate accuracy in Table 3. The RS, EA, and DiffCSP comparisons remain unchanged; FlowMM and EquiCSP are explicitly excluded, not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Existing splits, metrics, and main 50-step inference setting are retained. Appendix G introduces a single-sample integration-step sweep on 1,000 randomly selected test structures, while Appendix D compares batch constructions. The exact sweep is internally inconsistent: its text lists steps through 200, but Figure 7 includes points through 1,000.

E4.justification: The diagnostic evidence expands substantially. Appendix D tests batching efficiency and accuracy, Appendix G examines integration-step accuracy/runtime trade-offs, and Appendix H compares self-assembly scalability and runtime distributions, including initialization sensitivity. These address additional practical questions beyond v1's aggregate self-assembly ablation and existing scalability analysis.

E5.justification: Appendix H newly reports initialization-dependent variation in self-assembly trial-average runtime, ranging from 4.75 to 14.62 seconds, whereas v1 reports a single 4.75-second average. This is limited variability reporting: trial counts, seeds, and formal uncertainty estimates for prediction accuracy remain unspecified.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their results, but the appendices substantially expand reported outcomes. Table 10 adds Batch results of 32.73% match rate, 0.2743 RMSE, 332.74 GPU hours, and 0.19 seconds per structure, versus TimestepBatch's 31.69%, 0.2820, 1087.25 hours, and 1.94 seconds. Figures 7–8 add step-dependent results and self-assembly's advantage at larger block counts. Appendix H reports 27.14% self-assembly accuracy without reconciling it with the retained 30.04% in Table 3.

T1.justification: The revised loss definition introduces tangent-space rotation residuals, squared norms, and time weighting, constituting a substantive mathematical refinement rather than equivalent notation. Other flow definitions and PCA arguments are retained, including the material moved from Appendix D to E. No new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and retained concluding paragraph preserve the central claims: a generative model tailored to MOF structure prediction, rigid-building-block dimensionality reduction, and superior accuracy and efficiency with scalability to large structures. The headline 31.69% match-rate claim is unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive applicability limits concerning hypothetical-only evaluation, dependence on accurate known building blocks, and lack of periodic invariance. Appendices C–D acknowledge greater training cost than DiffCSP and explain slow convergence through effective batch size. Appendix H qualifies comparative scalability by recognizing self-assembly's advantage for larger block counts. These materially broaden the interpretation beyond v1's favorable summary.

D1.justification: Appendices C–D add GPU-memory ranges, detailed timing, Batch implementation information, and runtime-averaging instructions. Reported training times change from approximately seven days to 5d 2h for DiffCSP and 5d 15h for TimestepBatch, while v1's 15-epoch MOFFlow training count disappears. The code/checkpoint reference changes from anonymous hosting to a named GitHub repository.

R1.justification: v2 adds Albergo and Vanden-Eijnden (2023) and Liu et al. (2023), broadening attribution for flow-matching foundations beyond Lipman et al. It also adds Gibaldi et al. (2022) to contextualize building-block availability and explains resource-based exclusion of the already cited FlowMM and EquiCSP. Overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Edits are localized: Conclusion becomes Discussions, implementation prose is reorganized, terminology and captions are refined, and appendices are inserted and renumbered. Affiliations and publication headers change, acknowledgments are added, and the ethics statement is removed. Most existing narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is redrawn as a connected architecture diagram. Figures 7–8 and Tables 9–10 are added, while existing appendix tables and sections are consolidated and relocated. Several displayed equations become inline. The overall format and original benchmark displays remain largely unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the method and practical trade-offs easier to assess through the revised loss specification, batching and integration-step studies, resource reporting, and explicit limitations. The main benchmark evidence remains unchanged. Unreconciled self-assembly rates, the Figure 7 step-range discrepancy, and removal of the training epoch count limit the reproducibility gains. Overall, the added scrutiny and clearer applicability boundaries support a limited net improvement.
